newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Senior China representative visits Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Senior China representative visits Taiwan.

text.p: A senior Chinese official on Monday arrived in Taiwan for a nine-day visit, becoming the highest-level mainland representative to visit the island since Taipei-Beijing relations turned sour in 1995.

Liu Gangqi, deputy secretary-general of the semi-official Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Strait, told reporters after arriving in Taiwan that he and his delegation came here "just to attend a seminar".

Liu, whose group included some 30 Chinese scholars and experts, said he had been invited by the Taipei-based China Modernisation Promotion Foundation for a two-day seminar to discuss the modernisation of China.
The mainland association's Taiwan counterpart, the Straits Exchange Foundation, said it would host a banquet to welcome Liu.
"Our foundation vice chairman (Chiao Jen-ho) will invite them to a dinner tomorrow (Tuesday)," a Straits Exchange Foundation official told Reuters by telephone.
Local news media said Wu An-chia, vice chairman of Taipei's cabinet-level Mainland Affairs Council, would also attend the banquet. Wu's office declined comment.
Liu had said in late July that his Taiwan visit would be purely academic and could not mark a formal resumption of the semi-official contacts suspended by Beijing in 1995.

Cross-strait relations have remained chilly since 1995 after China, which views Taiwan as a rebel-held province, became enraged by a private trip made by Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui to the United States.
The trip prompted China to cancel semi-official contacts and launch several months of military sabre-rattling near the island.
Beijing's association and Taipei's Straits Exchange Foundation had represented the sides in previous semi-official talks in the absence of formal relations.
Taiwan and China split after a civil war in 1949.
